text:
tara: Quick sync — we need a concrete migration+SLA plan for v2 routes before the roadmap review tomorrow. Customers are asking about tool calling, structured outputs, and embeddings compatibility.

sanjay: Agreed. Main asks I'm hearing from sales: 1) minimal runtime regressions (latency/cost parity), 2) a clear opt-in migration path, 3) enterprise-safe deprecation timeline.

mike: For launch criteria I propose: latency within 10% of v1 on common seq lengths, regression tests for golden prompts (LLM QA), SDK shims that map v1 params -> v2, and a documented fallback strategy.

elaine: +1. Also add per-route telemetry so customers can see token cost delta and error rates post-migration.

samira: On embeddings: big customers need stable dims + deterministic hashing. If v2 changes dims, we must provide a reindex plan and a vector-compatibility shim for 6 months.

tara: Good. Let's be explicit about the migration playbook. Draft checklist: 1) announce timeline and migration guide, 2) SDK bump with opt-in header X-Redwood-API-Version: v2, 3) canary rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50%), 4) evaluation hooks and smoke tests, 5) rollback/auto-fallback policy.

mike: Canary numbers feel right. Suggest also: automatic fallback to v1-compatible model variant when a request triggers a structured-output schema failure.

sanjay: For deprecation window, legal/customer success prefer 6 months from GA announcement for non-enterprise, 12 months for enterprise with migration support. We should include monthly usage reports and migration checkpoints.

elaine: Rollout constraints: function-calling behavior changes are highest risk. We should treat function-calling as "opt-in advanced" at GA with explicit contract tests. Structured output strictness can be gradual: relaxed -> strict mode controlled by param.

samira: Example migration header we can document:

```
# client example
POST /v2/chat
Headers: {
  "Authorization": "Bearer <key>",
  "X-Redwood-API-Version": "v2",
  "X-Migration-Mode": "canary"
}
```

dev-rel-bot: :memo: Created draft migration guide in docs repo -> /internal/migrations/v2-draft (link in thread).

tara: Prioritization: we only ship the following at GA: chat/completions parity, basic function-calling (opt-in), embeddings with compatibility guarantees, reranking as a compatibility wrapper. Leave advanced structured output enforcement for a later minor release.

mike: That scope seems reasonable — reduces risk while covering customer asks.

sanjay: Pricing and SLA asks — product should propose token pricing parity for v2 GA and a latency SLO: 99th p50/p95 targets for standard routes. Ops: can we meet that with current serving runtime?

samira: From infra tests, p95 is within 8% for typical prompts on our benchmark rigs. We need a knob for customers to pin model variants to preserve latency for enterprise.

elaine: Next steps: PMs prepare a one-pager with launch criteria + migration timeline; eng to sign off on canary automation and fallback; docs to publish migration guide and SDK examples.

tara: Owners: PM: tara, Eng lead: mike, Infra/Canary: sanjay, Docs/DevRel: samira. Deadline: draft ready EOD Friday; final for review Monday.

tara: Any blockers? :thinking:

mike: Main blocker is test coverage for function-calling edge cases (tool args + streaming). I'll put up a ticket and tag eng-runtime.

samira: I'll coordinate quickstart code samples and a migration checklist for customers with large embeddings stores.

sanjay: I'll validate canary pipelines and add automatic reroute trigger if error rate delta > 2x baseline.

tara: Great — thanks everyone. I'll pull this into the roadmap doc and flag items for roadmap review. :white_check_mark:
